item.text: I’ve narrowed this to official docs plus current source files. Next I’m reconciling the generic-build docs with the Node-specific source behavior, because that is where the Bun implications come from.

Short answer: the current official PDF.js material does **not** clearly document the **generic modern build** as a recommended outside-browser target. What it **does** document is: the generic build for web use, a separate **Node.js** usage path, and several Node/runtime assumptions in source code that are directly relevant to **Bun**. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/README.md , https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/setup-pdf.js-in-a-website , https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/ , https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

**Supported facts**

- The official README says `npx gulp generic` builds the generic viewer, and generates `pdf.js` plus `pdf.worker.js` under `build/generic/build/`; it also says the “Modern browsers” version assumes native support for the latest JavaScript features. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/README.md
- The official setup wiki says official releases include “the generic build of PDF.js and the viewer,” and that `npx gulp generic` builds PDF.js from source into the `build` folder. https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/setup-pdf.js-in-a-website
- The official examples page says its tutorial is for using PDF.js “in a web browser,” and points separately to `examples/node/` for Node.js usage. https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/
- The official setup wiki’s NPM section points users to `examples/node/getinfo.mjs` as the usage example. https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/setup-pdf.js-in-a-website
- That official Node example imports `getDocument` from `pdfjs-dist/legacy/build/pdf.mjs`, not from the generic modern build. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs
- The same Node example loads a document with `getDocument({ url: pdfPath })`, iterates pages with `pdfDoc.getPage(i)`, extracts page text with `await pdfPage.getTextContent()`, and prints `items.map(item => item.str).join(" ")`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs
- In current source, `getTextContent` returns a `Promise<TextContent>`, while `streamTextContent` returns a `ReadableStream`; both note that whitespace is normalized to standard spaces, and the text-content parameters include `includeMarkedContent` and `disableNormalization`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js
- The current FAQ support matrix lists **Node.js 22+** only under the **`legacy` build**, marked “Mostly” supported with “Limited” automated testing. https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions
- Current source defines `isNodeJS` by checking for a real Node-style `process` object and explicitly excluding NW.js and Electron browser contexts. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/shared/util.js
- Current source force-disables workers when `isNodeJS` is true, with the comment “Workers aren't supported in Node.js,” and sets a default worker script path. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js
- In current `getDocument` setup, the Node-detected path defaults `isOffscreenCanvasSupported` to `false`, `isImageDecoderSupported` to `false`, `disableFontFace` to `true`, and `useSystemFonts` to `false`; it also defaults `ownerDocument` to `globalThis.document`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js
- In the generic build, when `isNodeJS` is true, current source selects `NodeCanvasFactory`, `NodeFilterFactory`, and `NodeBinaryDataFactory` by default. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js
- Current `node_utils.js` explicitly warns: “Please use the `legacy` build in Node.js environments.” https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js
- The same file assumes `process.getBuiltinModule("module").createRequire(import.meta.url)` is available, tries to `require("@napi-rs/canvas")`, polyfills `DOMMatrix` and `Path2D` from that package when possible, creates a fallback `globalThis.navigator` with `language: "en-US"` if needed, and reads files through `process.getBuiltinModule("fs/promises").readFile(...)`. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

**Inference relevant to Bun**

- If Bun is detected by PDF.js as `isNodeJS`, PDF.js will follow the Node path above: workers will be force-disabled, Node factories may be selected, and runtime success will depend on Bun behaving compatibly with `process`, `process.getBuiltinModule`, `createRequire(import.meta.url)`, `fs/promises`, and CommonJS loading of `@napi-rs/canvas`. This is an inference from current source structure, not an explicit PDF.js Bun support statement. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/shared/util.js , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js
- The official text-extraction path looks less coupled to canvas rendering than page rendering, because the Node text example uses `getTextContent()` and never renders a canvas. That said, this is still an inference about practical Bun behavior, not an explicit compatibility guarantee. https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs

**Disagreement / tension inside the official material**

- The docs broadly advertise a generic build and generic releases for web use, but the Node-specific example, the Node support matrix, and `node_utils.js` all steer outside-browser Node usage toward the **legacy** build instead of the generic modern build. Sources: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/README.md , https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/setup-pdf.js-in-a-website , https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/examples/node/getinfo.mjs , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

**Uncertainty / lack of good evidence**

- I found **no explicit Bun compatibility statement** in the official README, setup wiki, examples page, FAQ, `api.js`, `util.js`, or `node_utils.js`. That means any Bun conclusion has to be inferred from the Node-detection and Node-runtime assumptions above, rather than taken from an official PDF.js Bun support document. Sources reviewed: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/README.md , https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/setup-pdf.js-in-a-website , https://mozilla.github.io/pdf.js/examples/ , https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/wiki/frequently-asked-questions , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/api.js , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/shared/util.js , https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mozilla/pdf.js/master/src/display/node_utils.js

Net result: official PDF.js sources currently document **web generic build usage**, **Node text extraction via the legacy build**, and **Node-specific runtime assumptions** that matter for Bun, but they do **not** provide a direct official statement that the generic build is supported in Bun.
